chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from Sama'ah, from Abi Basir, who said:
I heard Aba Ja'far عليه السلام saying:

Indeed, the first thing by which the servant shall be called to account is the salat (prayer). If it is accepted, what is besides it is accepted; and indeed, when the salat rises at its time, it returns to its performer while it is white and radiant, saying: You preserved me, may Allah preserve you. And when it rises outside its time, without its proper limits, it returns to its performer while it is black and dark, saying: You neglected me, may Allah neglect you.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the obligatory salat (prayer), presented here as the first deed for which the servant is called to account
key_terms.بَيْضَاءُ مُشْرِقَةٌ: white and radiant, describing the prayer when properly observed
key_terms.حُدُودِهَا: its proper limits, requirements, and prescribed boundaries
key_terms.سَوْدَاءُ مُظْلِمَةٌ: black and dark, describing the prayer when neglected or improperly performed
key_terms.يُحَاسَبُ: is called to account or reckoned for

ai.seo_question: Why is salat (prayer) the first deed accounted for, and what happens if it is delayed or neglected?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that salat (prayer) is the foremost deed examined for a servant, and the acceptance of other deeds is tied to it. It emphasizes performing prayer on time and within its proper limits, portraying the prayer itself as bearing witness either in the worshipper's favor or against him.
